name: Tyhee Lake Provincial Park
note: Tyhee Lake Provincial Park campground on Tyhee Lake near Telkwa. Vehicle-accessible sites plus a groupsite and walk-in sites (walk-ins excluded); electrified sites available, sandy-beach day-use, EV chargers. Reservable online with some first-come, first-served sites. --Claude

name: Beaumont Provincial Park
note: Beaumont Provincial Park campground on the SE shore of Fraser Lake, 8 km west of Fort Fraser off Hwy 16. 49 vehicle-accessible tent/RV sites (many pull-through) plus 5 walk-in beach sites (excluded); no hookups, water spigots, boat launch, swimming. 16 sites reservable online, 33 first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Tudyah Lake Provincial Park
note: 36 vehicle-accessible open campsites plus a group site on Tudyah Lake, with a concrete boat launch and day-use area; no hookups, RV length limit ~32 ft (call ahead for larger rigs). First-come, first-served (reservations not accepted). --Claude

name: Meziadin Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks campground on the shore of Meziadin Lake off Hwy 37 (Stewart-Cassiar), 66 sites incl 18 with 30-amp electric, max RV ~32 ft; boat launch, dock, hand-pump drinking water. Reservable online; also first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Tā Ch'ilā Provincial Park (Boya Lake)
note: BC Parks (Tā Ch'ilā, formerly Boya Lake) campground on the west shore of turquoise Boya Lake, 2 km east of Hwy 37; 44 sites incl lakeside pull-throughs, no hookups; picnic shelter, playground, boat launch, cash only. Reservable online; also first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Liard River Hot Springs Provincial Park
note: BC Parks campground at Liard River Hot Springs on the Alaska Hwy, 53 gravel sites (21 reservable / 32 FCFS), no hookups, max RV ~32 ft; boardwalk to the natural hot springs; fills early each day in summer. Reservable online; also first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Muncho Lake Provincial Park - Strawberry Flats Campground
note: BC Parks campground on the shore of Muncho Lake at the south end of the park, right off the Alaska Hwy; 15 gravel sites, no hookups; 5 lakeshore sites reservable online, remaining 10 first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Muncho Lake Provincial Park - MacDonald Campground
note: BC Parks campground on the shore of Muncho Lake off the Alaska Hwy, ~11 km north of Strawberry Flats; 15 gravel sites, no hookups; 5 lakeshore sites reservable online, remaining 10 first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Summit Lake Campground (Stone Mountain Provincial Park)
note: BC Parks (Stone Mountain PP) campground on Summit Lake at the highest point on the Alaska Hwy (~1280 m), 28 large gravel sites big enough for RVs and trailers, no hookups; cash only. Some sites reservable online, rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Heather - Dina Lakes Provincial Park - Dina Lake Campsite
note: BC Parks. FCFS car campground at Dina Lake — 5 developed gravel-pad sites for tents, trailers and moderate-sized motorhomes (a larger grassy area at nearby Heather Lake takes bigger rigs). Access via Parsnip West FSR (gravel; 2WD-passable in summer, 4WD advised when wet); no potable water. --Claude

name: Buckinghorse River Wayside Provincial Park
note: BC Parks wayside on the Alaska Hwy (Hwy 97, ~km 278, ~200 km NW of Fort St John). 17 vehicle-accessible sites for RVs and tents, FCFS; pit toilets, picnic tables, fire pits. Open ~May-Sept. Non-potable water (boil). --Claude

name: Charlie Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks, 11 km N of Fort St John at the Alaska Hwy/Hwy 29 junction. 57 sites (elevated gravel pads, picnic table, fire ring; no hookups) — 40 reservable + 17 FCFS; cold water taps, pit toilets, sani-dump (fee), boat launch, playground, disc golf. Open ~May-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Moberly Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks, 25 km NW of Chetwynd off Hwy 29. 109 sites for RVs and tents (no hookups; RV length limit ~32 ft / 10 m) — 67 reservable + 42 FCFS; pit toilets, water taps, dump station, boat launch, playground. Open ~May-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Pine Le Moray Provincial Park, Heart Lake Campground
note: BC Parks, Hwy 97 ~71 km SW of Chetwynd. Heart Lake Campground has 13 FCFS sites (one double) suitable for tents and RVs of all sizes with some maneuvering (no pull-throughs, no hookups, no dump); 2 vault toilets, 2 water pumps (no drinking water), picnic tables, fire rings. Electric-motor-free lake. Open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Swan Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks frontcountry campground on Swan Lake, 27 km SE of Dawson Creek near Tomslake: 44 grassy drive-in sites (16 reservable, 28 first-come, first-served), no hookups, pit toilets, boat launch, dock, beach and ball diamonds. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Beatton Provincial Park
note: BC Parks campground on the east shore of Charlie Lake, 13 km NW of Fort St. John: 39 drive-in sites (27 reservable, 12 first-come, first-served) for RVs and tents, no hookups, pit toilets, boat launch and playground. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Illecillewaet Campground
note: Glacier NP at Rogers Pass; 60 unserviced sites (no hookups), flush toilets, potable water, kitchen shelters, food lockers, staffed welcome station. ~Half the sites reservable, half first-come, first-served. Sites for large RVs are limited but small RVs/vans fit; basecamp for nine Rogers Pass trailheads. Open ~mid-June to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Jordan River Regional Park
note: CRD (Capital Regional District) oceanfront regional park campground on Juan de Fuca Strait; 16 drive-in + 7 walk-in self-contained sites, no hookups, vault toilets. Open year-round, first-come first-served (cash only), 14-day annual max stay. --Claude

name: Centennial Campground and Park
note: Village of New Denver municipal campground on the shore of Slocan Lake, walkable to downtown. 44 drive-in sites: a treed loop with power/water and a lakeside area with no hookups/less shade; two bathhouses, sani-dump, boat launch, swimming beach. Primarily first-come, first-served. Open May 1-Sep 30. --Claude

name: Forest Rose Campground
note: Campground at Barkerville Historic Town & Park (a BC provincial heritage property operated by the Barkerville Heritage Trust) along the east side of Williams Creek near the Barkerville townsite; 56 sites (30 reservable / 26 FCFS), sites average 55 ft x 13 ft with pull-throughs, unserviced + 30-amp power, flush toilets/showers/potable water, playground. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Sunset RV Park & Campground
note: Village of Port Clements municipal campground at the south end of Sunset Park on the Yakoun River estuary (Masset Inlet), Haida Gwaii; 10 sites - 6 RV sites with electrical hookups + 4 tent - plus outhouses, potable water taps and a gazebo (sani-station in the village); open year-round. Reservable online or via the Village office, FCFS drop-in otherwise. --Claude

name: Riverside Municipal RV Park & Campground
note: Town of Smithers municipal campground on the Bulkley River; 43 sites with 15/30-amp electric, water and sewer hookups, flush toilets/showers, playground, camp kitchen, nature/bike trails; open ~May 15-Oct 1, 14-day max stay. Reservable online plus FCFS within 3 days of arrival. --Claude

name: White Swan Park Municipal Campground
note: Village of Fraser Lake municipal campground on the shore of Fraser Lake; ~6-8 pull-through plus similar back-in sites (pull-throughs ~75 ft), no hookups, washrooms, swimming beach and paddle-craft launch. 2-night limit, first-come first-served; railway runs alongside. --Claude

name: Fairy Lake Recreation Site
note: RSTBC Crown recreation site (managed by Silvifor) 5 km NE of Port Renfrew on Fairy Lake, via gravel Harris Main; 36 sites (16 reservable via VICamping, 16 FCFS), some large enough for RVs, sandy beach; rustic - pit toilets, no potable water, pack-in/out. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Maple Grove Recreation Site
note: RSTBC Crown recreation site (managed by Silvifor) on the north shore of Cowichan Lake near Youbou; ~82 lakeside sites (reservable + FCFS via VICamping, cash for FCFS), RV-accessible, pit toilets, boat launch, south-facing beach. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Telte-Yet Campsite
note: First Nations-owned riverfront campground on the Fraser River in downtown Hope (600 Water Ave); ~29 sites with 30-amp electric + water hookups, free hot showers, coin laundry, sani-dump. Generally first-come, first-served (no reservations). --Claude

name: Rustic Camping
note: Small riverside campground on the Similkameen River just west of Hedley off Hwy 3; gravel drive-in loop, flush toilets, drive-in sites used by RVers. First-come, first-served — cash via drop box. --Claude

name: Haywire Bay Regional Park
note: qathet Regional District park on the SE shore of Powell Lake, ~7 km from Powell River. 48 individual drive-in RV/tent sites plus 2 group sites; flush toilets, hot showers, boat launch, beach/day-use, playground. Single sites are first-come, first-served (not reservable) via a self-registration pay station. Open seasonally. --Claude

name: Noisy Creek Rec Site
note: RSTBC Crown recreation site REC1750 at the north end of Mabel Lake, ~20 km up Three Valley Gap FSR from Mabel Lake Rd. Sandy beach, camp host in high season, FCFS (no reservations). Most sites smaller — trailers over 26 ft not recommended (a 23-ft rig fits). No cell service. --Claude

name: Isobel Lake Recreation Site
note: RSTBC Crown recreation site REC4743 in the Lac du Bois grasslands ~40 min N of Kamloops off Lac du Bois FSR. 19 well-maintained flat sites, accessible outhouses, 3 km lakeshore trail; FCFS (14-day limit, no reservations). --Claude

name: Alexander Mackenzie's Landing Recreation Site
note: BC Hydro (Crown-utility-run) recreation site on Williston Reservoir, ~8 km by road from Mackenzie. 22-unit drive-in campground with sandy beach, boat launch and swimming; first-come first-served (no reservations), 14-night annual limit, open ~May 15-Oct 15. --Claude

name: Dease Lake Lions Tanzilla River Campground
note: Lions Club-run community campground on the Tanzilla River ~10 km S of Dease Lake on Hwy 37. Drive-in sites with picnic tables, fire pits, pit toilets, river-fishing and short trails; rustic/FCFS. --Claude

name: Townsite Campground
note: Parks Canada front-country campground at the south edge of Waterton townsite on the shore of Upper Waterton Lake; large open grassy campground with serviced (full/electric) and unserviced RV sites plus tent sites, fits most RVs. Reservable (Parks Canada) roughly May 8-Sep 21; FCFS in the early/late shoulder (May 1-8, Sep 22-Oct 12). Open ~May 1-Oct 12. --Claude

name: Wapiti Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Pkwy/Hwy 93A just S of Whistlers along the Athabasca River (~150 summer sites, reduced 2026); electrical (15/30/50-amp) and unserviced sites, accommodates most RV sizes. Summer season ~May 13-Oct 28 reservable; a ~40-site winter loop runs FCFS Oct 28-early May (electric only). --Claude

name: Snaring Campground
note: Jasper NP FCFS unserviced campground, 62 sites north of the townsite off Snaring Rd near the Snaring/Athabasca River; fire pits, no hookups or showers; Parks Canada lists sites for rigs under 27 ft (a 23-ft rig fits). First-come, first-served (mid-May to late Sept). Unaffected by the 2024 Jasper wildfire. --Claude

name: Honeymoon Lake Campground
note: Jasper NP FCFS unserviced campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93) at Honeymoon Lake, 34 sites; primitive (no hookups), rigs under 27 ft per Parks Canada. First-come, first-served (late May to mid-Sept). --Claude

name: Mount Kerkeslin Campground
note: Jasper NP FCFS unserviced campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93) ~36 km south of the townsite along the Athabasca River; 42 sites, primitive (fire rings, outhouses, no hookups), rigs under 27 ft per Parks Canada; sandy river bank with natural canoe launch. First-come, first-served (mid-May to mid-Sept). --Claude

name: Icefields Centre RV (Columbia Icefield)
note: Jasper NP FCFS overnight RV area at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93); ~100 primitive drive-in sites for self-contained RVs/trailers only, no water and no fires, elev ~1960 m. First-come, first-served (mid-May to mid-Oct). Separate from the adjacent tent-only Icefield walk-in campground. --Claude

name: Waterfowl Lakes Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway between Upper and Lower Waterfowl Lakes (Mistaya River), ~57 km N of Lake Louise. 110 unserviced sites, RVs/trailers to 9 m, sani-dump on site, first-come first-served only (non-reservable), open ~mid-Jun–early Sep. --Claude

name: Mosquito Creek Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway ~24 km N of Lake Louise, at Mosquito Creek. 38 unserviced sites, RVs/trailers to 10 m, first-come first-served only (non-reservable), open ~mid-Jun–mid-Oct. --Claude
